messages.text: I’m checking whether the shifted learning-curve interval reflects an implementation error or a limitation of the finite-training bootstrap, and what that means for the higher-statistics uncertainty estimates.

Reviewed **99eb9ed0587180873ca75e52a03e2dccf5440185**. **No implementation defect found; the bootstrap shift requires an interpretation caution.**

The 1k−8k width difference is **0.1317 percentage points**, while its bootstrap percentile range is **0.1570–0.5869 pp** and bootstrap SD **0.1135 pp**. Percentile endpoints are replicate quantiles; they need not bracket the observed estimate. Their exclusion of this estimate warns against treating the range as calibrated 95% significance evidence.

Retain the point and range unchanged. Finite-training reweighting, clipping and discrete model selection are plausible explanations, but this review does not establish the mechanism. Bootstrap interval accuracy can depend on bias treatment; see [Efron (1987)]([external URL redacted; see source journal]).

No estimator or bootstrap-method change is indicated before campaign evaluation. Before the final freeze, add centering diagnostics for full-bootstrap metrics and contrasts: bootstrap mean/median, mean-minus-point, fraction below the point and whether the point lies inside the central range. Keep conditional-validation intervals separate; report analogous full-bootstrap shifts explicitly.

Actual checks passed:

- All previous LC point metrics, intervals and metadata remain unchanged.
- Global **8×8** and angular **80×80** covariance ordering, symmetry and positive definiteness checked.
- Paired contrast point definitions agree exactly.

No new fits, bootstrap generation, validation inspection or writes. The LC remains exploratory; neither its small nonmonotonic changes nor these ranges establish an asymptotic training-data limit.
